question: What was Mendel’s contribution to genetics?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Laws of Inheritance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gregor Johann Mendel**, an Austrian monk and scientist, is universally recognized as the **Father of Genetics** for his groundbreaking work on the principles of heredity.
 
• Mendel conducted his famous experiments on **garden pea plants (Pisum sativum)** between the years **1856** and **1863**.
 
• Through his statistical analysis of breeding experiments, he proposed the fundamental **Laws of Inheritance**, which describe how traits are passed from one generation to the next through "factors" (now known as **genes**). ***Hence, the correct answer is Laws of Inheritance.***
 
• He published his findings in **1866** in a paper titled **"Experiments on Plant Hybridization"** (Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden), although his work remained largely unrecognized by the scientific community for several decades.
 
• Mendel's work provided the mathematical foundation for genetics, shifting the study of biology from purely descriptive to experimental and quantitative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Three Laws of Mendel:**
 
 
• **Law of Dominance**: This law states that in a cross of parents that are pure for contrasting traits, only one form of the trait (the **dominant**) will appear in the next generation. The hidden trait is known as **recessive**.
 
• **Law of Segregation**: It states that during the formation of **gametes** (egg or sperm), the two alleles for a trait separate, so that each gamete carries only one **allele** for each gene.
 
• **Law of Independent Assortment**: This principle states that the **alleles** of different genes separate independently of one another during the formation of gametes, meaning the inheritance of one trait does not influence the inheritance of another.
 
 
 
• **Pea Plant Characteristics:** Mendel chose **seven pairs** of contrasting traits in pea plants to study, including **stem height** (tall vs. dwarf), **seed shape** (round vs. wrinkled), and **flower color** (violet vs. white).
 
• **Monohybrid and Dihybrid Cross:** A **monohybrid cross** involves the study of one pair of contrasting traits, resulting in a phenotypic ratio of **3:1** in the F2 generation. A **dihybrid cross** involves two pairs of traits, resulting in a ratio of **9:3:3:1**.
 
• **Rediscovery:** Mendel’s laws were independently rediscovered in the year **1900** by three botanists: **Hugo de Vries**, **Carl Correns**, and **Erich von Tschermak**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Theory of Evolution:** This theory was primarily proposed by **Charles Darwin** in his **1859** work, **"On the Origin of Species,"** which introduced the concept of **natural selection**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Discovery of DNA:** While **Friedrich Miescher** first isolated DNA in **1869**, the **double-helix structure** was discovered by **James Watson** and **Francis Crick** in **1953**, using data from **Rosalind Franklin** and **Maurice Wilkins**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Inheritance of Acquired Traits:** This was a pre-Mendelian theory proposed by **Jean-Baptiste Lamarck** (Lamarckism), suggesting that physiological changes acquired during an organism's lifetime could be transmitted to offspring. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Genotype**: The genetic makeup of an organism (e.g., TT, Tt, tt).
 
• **Phenotype**: The observable physical characteristics (e.g., Tall or Dwarf).
 
• **Homozygous**: Having two identical alleles for a particular gene.
 
• **Heterozygous**: Having two different alleles for a particular gene.
